IRS Pub 1141 (tax year 2026) · Form W-2 employee copies · Pyramos

One sheet per employee: what Pub 1141 lets us print, what we must send, and the layout we picked

The IRS W-2 PDF is 11 pages and prints every copy twice per page, so it can't go in an envelope as is. Pub 1141 lets an employer print its own employee copies. This page explains what the rules allow, which pieces the employee must get, and why we chose a 4-up duplex sheet.

The two-sentence version

Each employee must get Copies B, C and 2 of their W-2 plus the IRS employee instructions. Pub 1141 lets us put all of that on one letter sheet if each copy keeps its required boxes and labels and the copies tear apart easily.

We picked a 4-up duplex sheet (B, C, 2, 2 on the front, instructions on the back) because it is the only layout we tried where all 2,058 words of the IRS back text fit.

The problem

Take one employee from our sample, Jordan Rivera at Zinnia Company in Philadelphia. In 2026 Jordan earned $58,000 in box 1, with PA state tax and a Philadelphia local tax.

Worked example · Jordan's W-2 printed from the IRS PDF
Pages in fw2.pdf11
Employees per page2 (each copy printed twice)
Pages Jordan needs (B, C, 2 + backs)6 pages, pages 4 to 9
Copy A from the PDFinformation only, can't be filed
With a Pub 1141 substitute1 sheet, printed both sides
Think of a concert ticket with tear-off stubs. One printout, and every stub goes somewhere different. Where this breaks: a stub only needs a seat number, but every W-2 copy has to stand alone as a full W-2, with boxes 1 to 6, the IDs, the title, the year and its own label. That rule is what limits the layout.

Which copies we must send

A W-2 set has six copies. Only three go to the employee, and the instructions must go with them.

CopyGoes toOur dutyPub 1141 basis
Copy BEmployee, for the federal returnMust send2.3.01, 2.3.10
Copy CEmployee, for their recordsMust send2.3.01, 2.3.18
Copy 2Employee, for a state, city or local returnMust send when the employee files one2.3.01 ("three or more")
Notice + instructionsEmployee, with the copiesMust send. The back of the sheet or a separate statement both count2.3.19, 2.3.20, 3.1.05
Copy ASSANever to the employee. We e-file it as an EFW2 file through BSO2.1, 2.2
Copy 1State or local tax departmentNever to the employee. Its back stays blank3.1.05
Copy DEmployer fileWe keep it, or can recreate it, for 4 years3.1.03
!
The rule in 2.3.01 says every employer must give each employee at least two copies, B and C. An employee who has to file a state, city or local return gets three or more. Jordan files with both PA and Philadelphia, so the second Copy 2 on our sheet is not wasted. Under Reg. 31.6051-1(j), employees who consent can get the copies electronically, and then there's no need for perforations.

What Pub 1141 allows, and what it requires

Section 2.3 covers employee copies only. Copy A follows stricter scanning rules that this sheet never has to meet.

Allowed

Room to design

  • Any size from 2.67 × 4.25 in to 6.5 × 8.5 in per copy, so a letter page holds up to four. 2.3.02
  • Horizontal or vertical format. A vertical copy can put boxes 1 to 6 across the top. 2.3.03 Exhibit F
  • All copies on a single sheet, as long as they separate easily. 2.3.05
  • Leave out boxes 7 to 14b and box d when they hold nothing for this employee. 2.3.08 2.3.14
  • More than four box 12 codes, and labeled extras in box 14a. 2.3.15 2.3.17
  • Truncated SSN (XXX-XX-4321). The "22222" number and the e-file logo can go. 2.3.07 2.3.08
  • Instructions on the back or on a separate statement. The backs of B and C alone are enough. 3.1.05
  • Edit the instructions: drop the parts that don't apply (railroad, dependent care) and change the font so the text fits. 2.3.19 2.3.20
Required

What every copy must carry

  • Boxes 1 to 6 in IRS order, in the upper right (or across the top for vertical), each at least 1⅛ × ¼ in. Nothing goes to their right. 2.3.08
  • Boxes a, b, c, e, f: SSN, EIN, employer, employee name and address. 2.3.08
  • "Form W-2", "Wage and Tax Statement" and the year together, plus "Department of the Treasury, Internal Revenue Service" on every copy. 2.3.09 2.3.11
  • The copy label, such as "Copy B, To Be Filed With Employee's FEDERAL Tax Return." 2.3.10
  • Copy B: boxes 1 and 2 outlined in a bold 2-point rule. 2.3.12
  • State and local boxes 15 to 20 at the bottom when we withhold those taxes. 2.3.13
  • Copy C front: the negligence-penalty note. 2.3.18
  • The EITC notice for employees with no income tax withheld, which the back of Copy B covers. 2.3.20
  • White paper, black ink, at least 9-pound stock, with copies easy to separate (perforations are best). 2.3.04 2.3.05

How we landed on the layout

We compared three options using the same employee (Jordan) and the same IRS back text (2,058 words from pages 5, 7 and 9 of fw2.pdf). The deciding question was one we could measure: does all the required text fit on the back?

Option 1 · Print the official IRS PDF rejected

This works only if a person fills it in by hand. Each page holds two employees, the copies are spread across six pages, and the PDF's Copy A can't be filed anyway.

Jordan, official fw2.pdf
Paper per employee6 pages (shared with a 2nd employee)
VerdictNot mailable per employee
Option 2 · Three horizontal strips (B, C, 2) rejected

This looks most like the official form. Each strip is 8.5 × 3.67 in, inside the allowed size. But a horizontal copy at that height squeezes the employer and employee address boxes, and the back has room for only three bands of text.

Jordan, 3-up, instructions at 6.4pt
Copy size8.5 × 3.67 in (allowed)
IRS back text placed1,837 of 2,058 words
Cut offBox 14a, Box 14b, "Keep Copy C" note
Verdict221 words short
Option 3 · 4-up duplex, vertical format (B, C, 2, 2) chosen

Each quarter page is 4.25 × 5.5 in, which is exactly the minimum width and well within the maximum height. Boxes 1 to 6 run across the top, as the vertical format in Exhibit F shows. Boxes 7 to 11 print only when they hold a value. The empty space above the state boxes leaves room for extra box 12 codes.

On the back, the Notice to Employee (with the EITC notice) sits behind Copy B. The Instructions for Employee start behind Copy C and continue behind the two Copy 2s. The page is flipped on the long edge, so the back mirrors the front's columns.

Jordan, 4-up, instructions at 6.4pt
Copy size4.25 × 5.5 in (allowed)
Boxes 1 to 6 sizeabout 1.9 × 0.3 in (min 1⅛ × ¼)
IRS back text placed2,058 of 2,058 words
Copy 2 count2, one each for PA and Philadelphia
VerdictEverything fits, nothing cut
How we checked. Both layouts were printed to PDF with headless Chrome. A script placed the instruction paragraphs and counted any words that didn't fit. We zoomed in to confirm the bold rule on Copy B, and checked that the values, the masked SSN, the Copy C note and the "Keep Copy C" note all appear in the PDF's text. This is a mockup with made-up data, not production code.

The plain-language rule

Mail each employee one letter sheet. The front has Copies B, C, 2 and 2. Each copy shows boxes 1 to 6 on top, the IDs, the state and local boxes at the bottom, the title and year, the IRS name and its own label. Copy B gets the bold box 1 and 2 outline, and Copy C gets the negligence note.

Print the IRS Notice to Employee behind Copy B and the instructions behind the others, and perforate between the copies.

Still open

  1. Where the real generator lives. One option is Java and PDFBox in returnpdf/, next to the 941 paper copies. The other is the W-2 work in claude-projects, which already has the employee data.
  2. Paper or electronic. Mailing needs perforated letter stock printed on both sides. Delivering a PDF needs each employee's consent under Reg. 31.6051-1(j) and skips the perforations.
  3. The second Copy 2. Keep it for employees with a state and a local return, like Jordan. If most employees file in one state only, leave that quarter blank.
